question: As part of the implementation of the EU Youth Strategy 2019-2027, it appears that a significant number of advisory bodies have been set up to represent young people in EU and national institutions.

This is the case for the long-term secretariat of the EU Youth Dialogue, for the Commission Youth Network of youth correspondents in each directorate-general, for the network of young professionals inside and outside the Commission, for the EU Youth Stakeholders Group and for the national youth councils. The role of those advisory bodies is to mainstream youth in the EU’s various policies.
However, for such bodies to represent young people, they still need to resemble the youth demographic and not exclude one section of that population. 1.
How are the members of those various networks and councils recruited?
Is that recruitment conditional on the plurality of political views and the diversity of social and geographical origin?
If not, has the Commission ensured that those advisory bodies will not interfere with electoral processes in the various Member States?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.10.2026) The EU Youth Strategy 2019-20271 aims to ensure that the views of young people are reflected in the development of the EU’s policies and programmes. Key to this is the implementation of a wide range of youth-led consultative initiatives which aim to strengthen youth mainstreaming in an inclusive manner.

The EU Youth Dialogue is Europe’s largest youth-centred consultation mechanism with up to 50 000 young people consulted in each 18-month period. Its secretariat is supported by the European Youth Forum, the biggest platform of youth organisations from across Europe.

As regards the EU Youth Stakeholders Group, at its launch in 2025, each Member State was invited to nominate a national representative, and the invitation was also extended to National Youth Councils. Also, the Commission published an open call for European youth organisations, and the final list is published on the European Youth Portal2.
The Commission’s Youth Network brings together Commission staff (experts in their fields) from across the Commission.
